channel.description: The FOX News Rundown is your daily news podcast for making sense of the big issues directly impacting your life. Go beyond the headlines every morning and join some of FOX News’ most exceptional journalists—including FOX News Channel reporters Peter Doocy, Aishah Hasnie, Bill Melugin, Alex Hogan, Lucas Tomlinson and Jacqui Heinrich and FOX News Radio reporters Dave Anthony, Jessica Rosenthal, Lisa Brady, and Gurnal Scott - as they tap into the global reporting resources of FOX News and get unparalleled political analysis and exclusive insight from top newsmakers. The Rundown offers a sharp contrast of perspectives you won’t hear anywhere else, and a daily commentary you can't miss, we deliver the full picture of the day's biggest events.

item.title: “We’re All Going to Die”!? Neil deGrasse Tyson on Space Mysteries, Aliens & AI
item.description:
Some strange things are happening out in space and down here on Earth.
Earlier this week, astrophysicist Neil deGrasse Tyson joined Aishah Hasnie to unpack a fast-moving object known as 1998 KY26 orbiting the Sun, UAP discussions, and the physics behind what a first alien encounter might actually look like. Tyson broke down why its trajectory doesn't follow standard gravity alone, weighed theories ranging from space junk to the Yarkovsky effect, and shared insights from his book Take Me to Your Leader: Perspectives on Your First Alien Encounter.
They also dove into growing concerns around artificial intelligence, tech vulnerabilities, and why Tyson says global guardrails are essential—plus why he’d choose the future if he had a time machine.
The conversation was full of laughs and interesting perspectives on space and the potential for extraterrestrial life, but it was too long for our regular midweek Rundown. So, on today's FOX News Rundown: Extra, we'll let you hear the whole conversation with Neil deGrasse Tyson and more of his unique takes on the galaxy. Learn more about your ad choices. item.title: Three Superpowers, One Room: What Came Out of Shenzhen?
item.description:
Following President Trump’s trip to Asia and a first-ever trilateral meeting with the leaders of China and Russia, foreign policy experts are weighing what was accomplished on the world stage. Former national security advisor to Vice President Dick Cheney and Heritage Foundation senior research fellow Stephen Yates joins The Rundown to analyze the summit’s outcomes on Taiwan, Ukraine, Iran, and strategic arms talks. Yates also explains how new rare-earth agreements with U.S. allies and export controls on AI chips balance Trump’s warmer rhetoric toward Beijing.
Later, widespread tech outages across major platforms and government systems raise urgent questions about whether U.S. digital infrastructure is prepared for the artificial intelligence era. Former Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) director Bridget Bean breaks down how rapid software patching can trigger cascading system failures, the growing cyber threats posed by China and Iran, and how organizations can defend against weaponized AI tools. item.title: What We Know About the Investigation into Rep. Ilhan Omar
item.description:
Rep. Ilhan Omar’s (D-MN) immigration history is facing fresh scrutiny after federal agents searched her Washington, D.C., home in October, with new reports detailing subpoenas to relatives. There are also reports that her congressional staffers have been requested to speak about the possibility they were told to change the birth year listed in public biographies. This week, a federal judge in Washington, D.C. may have paved the way for the way to unseal the criminal search warrant and related documents against Rep. Ilhan Omar. Where do we stand on this investigation?
FOX's Alexis McAdams speaks with Minnesota Republican Congressman Tom Emmer who says this isn't about background or beliefs, it is about facing consequences for criminal activity.

item.title: They Won Big. Can Democrats Actually Get Anything Done?
item.description:
Following sweeping midterm victories that are reshaping the balance of power in Washington, Democrats are already facing a fierce intraparty battle over leadership & leverage. FOX News Sunday Anchor and Host of the Livin’ the Bream Podcast Shannon Bream joins to discuss Hakeem Jeffries’ path to the Speaker’s gavel, Senate leadership dynamics involving Chuck Schumer, Chris Van Hollen, and John Fetterman’s 2028 outlook, and how a multi-day NSA outage and President Trump’s push for bipartisan deals could test both national security and party loyalty.
Astrophysicist Neil deGrasse Tyson joins White House correspondent Aishah Hasnie to investigate 1998 KY-26, a mysterious object orbiting the sun whose trajectory isn’t following standard laws of gravity. Drawing from his new book, Take Me to Your Leader: Perspectives on Your First Alien Encounter, Tyson explains how humans could use math to communicate with extraterrestrials and challenges congressional UFO whistleblowers to bring forward hard evidence. He also addresses growing vulnerabilities around artificial intelligence, warning that the United States, China, and Russia must agree on guardrails to keep AI from becoming our overlords.
PLUS, commentary by Dr. Marc Siegel, the Senior Medical Analyst for FOX News.
